title: Niche topics (2): prices, curves, spreads and ladders
objectives: Explain clean vs dirty price and the yield curve.
Say why Macaulay duration matches a goal date and modified duration estimates swings.
body_md:
Clean price excludes accrued interest; dirty price includes it and is what the buyer actually pays — which explains why the cash paid differs from the quoted price. The yield curve plots yields against maturities: normal means longer pays more; flat or inverted means little or no extra pay for longer. Credit spread is the extra yield a corporate bond pays over a G-sec of the same maturity; a wider spread means the market sees more risk. Roll-down: as a bond nears maturity, its price usually moves towards face value. Macaulay duration is the weighted-average time to receive cash flows (used for SEBI categories); modified duration is price sensitivity to a 1% rate change. A bond ladder spreads money across bonds or FDs maturing in different years, smoothing reinvestment risk.

| Topic | What it is | Why it matters to the client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clean vs dirty price | Clean price excludes accrued interest; dirty price includes it and is what the buyer actually pays | Explains why the cash paid differs from the quoted price |
| Yield curve | Yields plotted against maturities. Normal = longer pays more; flat or inverted = little or no extra pay for longer | Tells you whether locking in a longer maturity is being rewarded |
| Credit spread | Extra yield a corporate bond pays over a G-sec of the same maturity | Wider spread = market sees more risk |
| Roll-down | As a bond nears maturity, it moves down the yield curve and its price usually moves towards face value | Part of how target maturity funds deliver close to their starting YTM |
| Macaulay vs modified duration | Macaulay: weighted-average time to receive cash flows (used for SEBI categories). Modified: price sensitivity to a 1% rate change | Use Macaulay to match the goal date, modified to estimate price swings |
| Bond ladder | Spreading money across bonds or FDs maturing in different years | Smooths reinvestment risk and gives regular maturities for income |
example: Quoted ₹1,000, paid ₹1,017: the difference is accrued interest — the dirty price is what the buyer actually pays.
say: Use Macaulay to match the goal date, modified to estimate price swings.
A wider credit spread means more perceived risk.
never: The quoted price is always what you pay.
A flat yield curve rewards lending longer.
